title: Damascus / Baghdad
hook: 600 → 800. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Damascus / Baghdad in 600 and 800, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 600 and 800; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Damascus area anchor: 36.29, 33.51 (0 km from the nominal location); Baghdad area anchor: 44.37, 33.32 (0 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 600 and 800 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["Eastern Roman Empire"],["Sasanian Empire"]],[["Abbasid Caliphate"],["Abbasid Caliphate"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_600.geojson (SHA-256 e8d285de5d4257c55158979e866191d13464abc74e3082fb5f2065b357beec7a); GeoJSON features [[189],[43]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_800.geojson (SHA-256 9d046cdc4662109c3f803ae46e2c8cba941aa092ec86eccc7823e6cf1554920c); GeoJSON features [[33],[33]]

claims.text: At the two points, 600 has different labels and 800 has same label. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_600.geojson (SHA-256 e8d285de5d4257c55158979e866191d13464abc74e3082fb5f2065b357beec7a); GeoJSON features [[189],[43]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_800.geojson (SHA-256 9d046cdc4662109c3f803ae46e2c8cba941aa092ec86eccc7823e6cf1554920c); GeoJSON features [[33],[33]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: A map gives two places one label. Does that establish that their inhabitants shared one language? Answer: No, a map label does not establish language A territorial label describes this map's classification, not the languages of everyone within it.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[0]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
